results.content: In Islam Observed: Religious Development in Morocco and Indonesia, the anthropologist Clifford Geertz demonstrated the extent to which cultural anthropology can recount and revisit social formulations of religions and thus reopen new horizons and positionalities in understanding and perceiving religion practices by employing a comparative methodology that combines disciplines of anthropology, ethnography, sociology, and literature. results.title: Ethics and Aesthetics in Islamic Heritage
results.content: Drawing on historical, cultural, and artistic examples, this Congress aims to explore questions such as the interconnection between ethics and aesthetics in Islamic heritage, the application of aesthetic values in daily life, the instrumentalization of art for purposes of power or religious exclusivism, the integration of art as a space for encountering the Other, theological reflections for an ethics concerned with a heritage hospitable to alterity, and the reconciliation of creative freedom with ethical responsibility.
